title: Not Learning
note: This means the lowness that comes of not learning. Praising learning wasn’t enough on its own, so it is shown from the other side as well, after the chapter on learning.

couplets.plain: Speaking in an assembly without having studied fully is like playing at counters with no board.
couplets.pm: To speak in an assembly without having learned the books that would make you complete is like rolling counters without first marking out the board. Being complete means knowing all that needs knowing. Neither your words nor your meaning will follow any order.

links.reason: Without study a speaker has no ground to move on, as counters have none without a board.
Speaks of the one who holds forth in an assembly, and of what they lack if unread.

couplets.plain: An unlearned man’s desire to speak is like a woman with no breasts at all desiring womanhood.
couplets.pm: An unlearned man wanting to speak in an assembly is like a woman born with no breasts at all wanting womanhood. The want won’t reach its end, and if it does it will only bring laughter.
couplets.sensitive: mocks a woman's body to make its point

links.quote: An unlearned man’s desire to speak
links.reason: Ridicules the unlearned man’s wish to speak when he has nothing to speak with.

couplets.plain: Even the unlearned are very good, if they can keep from speaking in front of the learned.
couplets.pm: Even the unlearned are very good if they know themselves and can stay silent in an assembly of the learned. They don’t know themselves, so this is unlikely, which is why it says “if”. If they manage it they won’t expose themselves, and they may come to want learning.

links.quote: if they can keep from speaking in front of the learned

couplets.plain: Even when an unlearned man’s cleverness is very good, the wise don’t accept it.
couplets.pm: Even if an unlearned man’s intelligence happens at times to be very good, the wise don’t count it as intelligence. It can’t be good, and if it is, that is mere chance, like letters traced in sand by a snail. So those with settled knowledge of the books pay it no regard.

couplets.plain: An unlearned man’s standing falls away when he comes face to face with others and speaks.
couplets.pm: The self-regard of a man who hasn’t learned, who thinks himself wise, collapses when he meets a learned man and talks with him. It lasts only until he says something. Once he speaks he blunders, and it is gone.

links.quote: falls away when he comes face to face with others and speaks
An unlearned man’s standing falls away

couplets.plain: All you can say of the unlearned is that they exist. They are like salt land that yields nothing.
couplets.pm: The unlearned can be seen, so some will say they exist, and no more. They are like salt land that grows nothing, of no use to themselves or to others. Such land is neglected and gives no creature food, and they are given no regard and give no one knowledge.

links.reason: Pictures the unlearned as salt land that yields nothing.

links.quote: All you can say of the unlearned is that they exist
links.reason: Leaves them nothing but bare existence, alive in name and no more.

couplets.plain: The fine looks of a man with no subtle, searching mind are like those of a well-made clay doll.
couplets.pm: The bearing and beauty of a man without a fine, excellent mind that has entered many books are like those of a doll skilfully made of plaster. An excellent mind grasps things quickly and doesn’t forget. A handsome body is rare and is some benefit, but without learning it counts for nothing.

links.quote: like those of a well-made clay doll

couplets.plain: Wealth in the hands of the unlearned is worse than poverty falling on the good.
couplets.pm: Wealth with the unlearned is worse even than poverty with the learned. Each is out of its proper place, and both bring trouble to those who have them and suffering to the world. But wealth ruins the unlearned, while poverty doesn’t ruin the good, so wealth is the worse.

links.quote: Wealth in the hands of the unlearned
links.reason: Puts wealth with the unlearned below poverty with the good.

couplets.plain: The unlearned, though born high, don’t have the standing of the learned, though born low.
couplets.pm: The unlearned, though born into a high caste, lack the greatness of the learned, though those are born into a low one. The height of caste ends with the body, while the height of learning goes on with the soul, so it is greater. Caste pride is of no use to the unlearned.

links.reason: Denies the unlearned any shelter in a high birth.

links.quote: the standing of the learned, though born low
links.reason: Lets learning lift those born low above those born high.
Places the learned by their learning alone, however low their birth.

couplets.plain: As beasts are to humans, so others are to those who have learned bright books.
couplets.pm: However much better humans are than beasts, that much worse are the unlearned than those who have learned shining books. The understanding that raises humans above beasts is seen only in the learned, so the two aren’t of the same birth. The unlearned gain nothing from being born human.

links.reason: Sets the distance between learned and unlearned equal to that between humans and beasts.
